title: Comparatives 2: The Four You Must Memorise (лучше, хуже, больше, меньше)
titleRussian: Сравнительная степень 2: Четыре формы наизусть (лучше, хуже, больше, меньше)
description: Four of the most common Russian comparatives are completely irregular and cannot be built by rule: хороший → лучше, плохой → хуже, большой → больше, маленький → меньше. Learn them as fixed words.
descriptionRussian: Четыре самых частых русских сравнительных формы — полностью неправильные, их нельзя построить по правилу: хороший → лучше, плохой → хуже, большой → больше, маленький → меньше. Их учат наизусть как готовые слова.
intro: Four of the most useful comparatives in the language are completely irregular, and there is nothing to derive. Better, worse, more and less are their own words. Two of them double as everyday quantity words, which is why you will have met them long before this lesson. The one thing to avoid is stacking a second 'more' in front of them.
rules: Four comparatives are completely irregular and must be memorised as separate words: хороший → лучше (better), плохой → хуже (worse), большой → больше (bigger), маленький → меньше (smaller).
These four forms never change. One form fits any subject, whether masculine, feminine, neuter, or plural.
Больше also means 'more' and меньше also means 'less / fewer' as everyday quantity words.
Never say более лучше or более хороший. The single word лучше already means 'better,' so adding более is wrong.
examples: Сегодня погода лучше. (The weather is better today.) хороший → лучше.
Этот фильм хуже. (This film is worse.) плохой → хуже.
Москва больше. (Moscow is bigger.) большой → больше.
Эта комната меньше. (This room is smaller.) маленький → меньше.
У меня больше времени. (I have more time.) больше as 'more.'
Ешь меньше сахара. (Eat less sugar.) меньше as 'less.'

tables.title: The four irregular comparatives to memorise

items.hint: What is the comparative of хороший? It is a completely separate word.
items.explanation: Лучше is the irregular comparative of хороший ('good'). It is its own word, not built from хорош-.

items.promptEnglish: This film is worse, I don't recommend it.
items.hint: What is the comparative of плохой? It does not contain плох-.
items.explanation: Хуже is the irregular comparative of плохой ('bad'). You learn it as a separate word; it does not contain плох-.

items.promptEnglish: Moscow is bigger than my town.
items.hint: What is the comparative of большой? The same word also means 'more.'
items.explanation: Больше is the irregular comparative of большой ('big'): one fixed word, learned by heart, that never changes.

items.promptEnglish: My room is smaller than yours.
items.hint: What is the comparative of маленький? The same word also means 'less.'
items.explanation: Меньше is the irregular comparative of маленький ('small'): one fixed word, learned by heart, that never changes.

items.prompt: У Антона _____ времени, чем у меня.
items.promptEnglish: Anton has more time than I do.
items.hint: Here the meaning is 'more.' Which of the four words doubles as 'more'?
items.explanation: Больше also works as the everyday word for 'more': больше времени ('more time').

items.prompt: Этот рюкзак _____ и легче, удобно носить.
items.promptEnglish: This backpack is smaller and lighter, comfortable to carry.
items.hint: We need 'smaller,' the comparative. Which single word is it?
items.explanation: Меньше is the comparative of маленький ('small'), so it means 'smaller.'

blanks: Эта книга _____, чем фильм. (This book is better than the film.)
Зимой дни _____. (In winter the days are shorter, smaller.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Both answers are irregular comparatives you memorise as separate words. Лучше = 'better' (from хороший); меньше = 'smaller / shorter / less' (from маленький).
explanations: Лучше is the irregular comparative of хороший. The plain adjective хороший just means 'good,' not 'better.'
Меньше is the irregular comparative of маленький; here it means the days are 'smaller / shorter.' Маленькие is just the plain adjective 'small.'

errorCorrection.sentence: Этот хлеб более хороший, чем тот в магазине.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This bread is better than the one in the store.
errorCorrection.explanation: Хороший has a completely separate comparative that you memorise: лучше ('better'). Более хороший ('more good') copies the English pattern, but Russian rejects it because the single word лучше already exists.

errorCorrection.sentence: Сегодня я чувствую себя более плохо.
errorCorrection.explanation: The comparative of плохой / плохо is the separate word хуже ('worse'). Более плохо ('more badly') is wrong because Russian uses the ready single word хуже.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Moscow is bigger than Saint Petersburg.
errorCorrection.explanation: The comparative of большой is the fixed word больше ('bigger'). Большее looks like a regular -ее form, but большой does not build that way; больше is just learned as a unit.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This apartment is smaller than mine.
errorCorrection.explanation: The comparative of маленький is the separate word меньше ('smaller'). Маленее is not a real word; learners invent it by adding -ее to the stem, but маленький does not work that way.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: This restaurant is worse than that one.
minimalPairs.explanation: Хуже is the irregular comparative of плохой and means 'worse.' Плохой is just the plain adjective 'bad'; it does not express 'worse.' The comparative is the separate word хуже, learned by heart.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The new apartment is bigger than the old one.
minimalPairs.explanation: Больше is the irregular comparative of большой and means 'bigger.' Большая is just the plain adjective 'big' in the feminine; it does not mean 'bigger.' Use the fixed form больше for the comparison.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each word: is it a comparative ('better / worse / bigger / smaller') or just a plain adjective?

sentenceBuilding.hint: Use the irregular comparative of хороший. It never changes form.
Use the irregular comparative of маленький.
Use the irregular comparative of плохой. The comparative word itself does not change.
Here больше works as the everyday word for 'more.'

reviewVocab.definition: better (the irregular comparative of хороший; one fixed word that never changes, used for any subject)
worse (the irregular comparative of плохой; one fixed word that never changes)
reviewVocab.example: Этот фильм хуже, я не советую.

reviewVocab.definition: bigger / more (the irregular comparative of большой; also the everyday word for 'more')
reviewVocab.example: Москва больше, и у меня больше времени там.

reviewVocab.definition: smaller / less (the irregular comparative of маленький; also the everyday word for 'less, fewer')
reviewVocab.example: Эта комната меньше, ешь меньше сахара.
